passages.title: Dialogue 1: A new café
passages.text:
Woman: Have you been to that new café on Market Street yet?
Man: Yes, I went on Saturday with my sister. The cakes were lovely, and to be honest, the prices weren't bad for the size of them.
Woman: I heard it gets really busy.
Man: It was full, but they keep the music quiet, so we could chat easily. The problem was that we waited forty minutes for two coffees. There were only two people working there. I won't go back until they've got more staff.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: A school trip
passages.text:
Boy: Are you coming on the trip to the science museum on Friday?
Girl: I have to. It's part of the course. I don't mind museums, and science is one of my favourite subjects, so that's not the problem.
Boy: Is it the early start? The coach leaves at seven.
Girl: No, that's fine. It's just that they've chosen the day of my swimming final. I've been training for months, and now I'm going to miss it. It's so unfair. Why couldn't they pick another day?

passages.title: Dialogue 3: Cycling to work
passages.text:
Man: Since I started cycling to work, I feel so much fitter.
Woman: Me too. I sleep better, and I've got loads more energy. I'm not sure it saves me any money, though. I spent a fortune on the bike and all the clothes.
Man: Really? I think I save loads on petrol.
Woman: Maybe. And for me it's slower than the car. It takes me twice as long.
Man: Not for me. The traffic on my road is terrible in the mornings, so I get there much faster on my bike.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: A TV series
passages.text:
Man: Did you finish that crime series you were watching?
Woman: No, I stopped after four episodes.
Man: Oh? I thought the actors were supposed to be really good.
Woman: They were. The woman who played the detective was brilliant. And it wasn't about time. I was on holiday, so I had plenty of it. But there were so many characters, and it kept jumping backwards and forwards in time. By episode four, I had no idea what was going on, so I gave up.

passages.title: Dialogue 5: A phone call about tonight
passages.text:
Girl: Hi, Ben, it's Lucy. It's about tonight.
Boy: Hi, Lucy. Is everything OK?
Girl: Yes, but you know we were going to see the film at seven? I have to help my mum in the shop after work, so could we go to the nine o'clock one instead? Oh, and don't worry about your bike. My brother fixed mine yesterday, so I don't need to borrow it any more.
Boy: Nine's fine with me. See you at the cinema.

passages.title: Dialogue 6: A new phone
passages.text:
Man: Is that your new phone? What do you think of it?
Woman: Well, it cost less than I expected because it was in the sale. And it's really simple to use. I set it up in five minutes. But the photos are nothing like the ones in the adverts. In the evening, they all come out dark and blurry.
Man: That's a shame. The camera was the main reason you chose it.
Woman: Exactly. I feel a bit let down, to be honest.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a new café. What does the man dislike about it?
options: b) The prices are too high.
c) The service is too slow.
questions.explanation: The man says "we waited forty minutes for two coffees" and he won't go back "until they've got more staff", so the problem is the slow service. He says the prices "weren't bad" and the music is quiet, so it is not too expensive or noisy.

questions.question: You will hear two students talking about a school trip. How does the girl feel about the trip?
options: c) Nervous about the early start
questions.explanation: The girl is upset because "they've chosen the day of my swimming final" and says "It's so unfair. Why couldn't they pick another day?" She says the early start is "fine" and science is one of her favourite subjects.

questions.question: You will hear two colleagues talking about cycling to work. What do they agree about?
options: a) It is quicker than going by car.
b) It is good for their health.
questions.explanation: The man says he feels "so much fitter" and the woman replies "Me too", adding that she sleeps better and has more energy. They disagree about money (she spent a fortune on the bike) and about speed (it is slower for her but faster for him).

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a TV series. Why did the woman stop watching it?
options: a) She found the story confusing.
b) She didn't like the actors.
c) She didn't have enough time.
questions.explanation: She says there were so many characters and it kept jumping in time, so "I had no idea what was going on, so I gave up". She thought the actors were good ("brilliant") and she had plenty of time on holiday.

questions.question: You will hear a girl phoning a friend. Why is she calling him?
options: b) To ask to borrow something
c) To invite him to the cinema
questions.explanation: Lucy asks "could we go to the nine o'clock one instead?", so she wants to change the time they arranged. She says she doesn't need to borrow his bike any more, and the cinema trip was already planned, so it is not a new invitation.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a new phone. What does the woman think about it?
options: a) It is difficult to set up and use.
b) It cost more than she had expected.
questions.explanation: She says the photos are "nothing like the ones in the adverts" and come out "dark and blurry", and she feels "let down". It cost less than she expected and she says it is "really simple to use".
